span: From Ðā ongunnon twā ðēoda through and hīe mid ealle foriermdon. No following appeal assigned.
translations: Then two peoples began to attack them—the Picts from the north and the Scots from the west—and to seize and ravage their possessions; and they afflicted and humbled them for many years. Then, in that turmoil, they sent messengers to Rome with letters and a tearful petition; they asked them for help and promised them willing obedience and continual submission if they would help them so that they could overcome their enemies.

Then they sent them a large army to help, and as soon as they came to this island, they fought against their enemies and inflicted great slaughter on them, and drove them out of their borders and put them to flight; and they instructed them to make a fortification for their protection against their enemies; and thus they went home with great victory.

When the former enemies realized that the Roman army had gone away, they immediately came with a fleet to their borders, and slew and killed all whom they encountered, and trampled and destroyed them like ripe crops, and utterly devastated them.
interpretive_checks: First attackers are Picts/Scots; the sufferers and petitioners are Britons. Roman recipients become the subject sending relief, and legionaries perform the subsequent fighting and withdrawal. Pronouns require contextual referent tracking.
The formal Roman sending clause is active despite a passive in the underlying Latin, as Cook146 note3 explicitly states. Do not silently turn active syntax into a passive parsing answer.

Gewiten follows wæs and belongs to an intransitive depart verb; the withdrawal precedes the recognition and renewed attack. English had gone away preserves that relation; was gone may preserve the resulting state.
The source uses coordinated near-synonyms. Natural translation may combine paired verbs, but exact graded analysis must retain their separate forms and roles.
Genǣru belongs to the Britons; final slaughter applies to those encountered. The historical crop simile is retained, not expanded into invented details.
Full source transcription, original notes and local supports remain separate audit responsibilities; this witness is an independent translation, not the learner key.
